text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley, who is visiting Brazil, has rejected accusations by the government that the U.S. is restricting market access to a number of Brazilian goods, saying the U.S. economy was the most open in the world.
Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN posted a net profit rise of 191 percent in the first quarter of this year in comparison with the same period last year, according to inflation adjusted results.
-- DEPUTY SAYS RECEIVED 200,000 REAIS FOR RE-ELECTION VOTE

Five deputies from the northern state of Acre were allegedly paid off by governors to vote in favor of a constitutional amendment which allos President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election.

President Cardoso said the creation of the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA) depended much more on the rich countries' in the north capacity to open their markets than on the South's willingness to integrate.
The chairman of Brazilian steelmaker CSN, Benjamin Steinbruch, has been voted in by shareholders as the new chairman of privatized mining giant CVRD.
-- GOVT THINKS IT HAS VOTES TO APPROVE CIVIL SERVICE REFORM
The government will be taking up again the voting of its civil service reform bill in the Chamber of Deputies and believes it has enough votes in favor to approve it.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
